sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 5.4% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F177].
Revenue fell 32.5% in FY2020 to $94.5 billion, then rose 64.7% in FY2021 and 51.5% in FY2022 to $236 billion [F5][D153][F6][D192][F7][D232].
The FY2022 jump came from higher upstream realizations and downstream margins [P57].
Revenue then declined three straight years, by 16.5% in FY2023, 1.8% in FY2024 and 4.6% in FY2025 to $184 billion [F8][D274][F9][D316][F10][D358].
The FY2025 decline reflected lower crude oil and refined product prices, partly offset by higher volumes [P17].
Chevron U.S.A. Inc. supplied 75.1% of FY2025 revenue and subtracted 3.9pp from growth [D402][D404].
Tengizchevroil was the offset, at 11.6% of revenue and +1.5pp of growth [D418][D420].
U.S. upstream revenue grew 34.0% in FY2025 and contributed +2.5pp, lifting its share to 10.6% [D553][D554][D552].
Worldwide production rose 12% on the Hess acquisition and growth at TCO, the Permian and the Gulf of America [P28].
Net income fell 30.5% against a 4.6% revenue decline, so there was no operating leverage [F20][D359][F10][D358].
Net margin was 6.7% in FY2025, below the 7.9% window median and far under the 15.1% FY2022 high [F30][D613][D612].
Net margin fell 2.5pp in FY2025, while operating costs fell 3.4% against a 4.6% revenue decline [D369][D373][D358].
Higher upstream depreciation, lower realizations and higher operating costs drove the earnings decline [P9].
Depreciation, depletion and amortization rose on higher production and higher rates [P12].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.8% from 35.5%, widening the gap between operating and net margin [D345][D303].
Operating cash flow of $33.9 billion was 2.76x net income, above the 1.35x free-cash-flow-to-net-income median of three energy peers [F60][F20][D346][D640].
Higher TCO distributions and legacy Hess assets more than offset lower commodity prices [P6].
Free cash flow was $16.6 billion, an 8.8% margin against a 8.9% median, with capex at 9.2% of revenue [F80][D343][D616][D342].
Capex was 0.86x D&A, so spending stayed below the depreciation charge [D348].
Net cash turned positive at $4.0 billion in FY2025 from net debt of $156 million, helped by $11.4 billion of debt issued [D351][D309][X157].
Net cash was 2.1% of revenue, the 83rd percentile of six energy peers against a -7.7% median [D352][D637][D638].
Buybacks of $12.1 billion plus dividends of $12.8 billion were 149.7% of free cash flow [X132][X142][D354].
The diluted share count still rose 2.1% in FY2025 [D374].
Revenue has fallen for three consecutive years, FY2023 through FY2025 [R1][F8][F9][F10].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, reaching 149.7% in FY2025 [R4][D270][D312][D354].
The revenue basis is inconsistent: FY2025 is $184 billion in the table versus $189 billion as first reported [R3][F10][X10].
Non-U.S. downstream was 34.9% of revenue and fell 13.1% in FY2025 [R6][D517][D518].
Watch whether net margin recovers toward the 7.9% median from 6.7% in the FY2026 10-K [D613][F30].
Watch whether buybacks plus dividends fall back toward the 59.1% of free cash flow seen in FY2022 from 149.7% in FY2025 [D354][D228].
Watch whether capex stays within the $18-19 billion 2026 guidance against $17.3 billion in FY2025 [P4][F70].
